name: Corsican Blue
lede: Corsican Blue is a moderate purplish blue from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, and like most of their place names, the dictionary does not say what on Corsica it was meant to match.

sections.title: A place name, unexplained
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul catalog Corsican Blue at #454172 on plate 45, row H, column 12 of their 1930 dictionary, dating its first recorded use to 1928 [1]. The same volume also lists a related swatch they call Intense Blue on plate 45, row F, column 12, a close cousin by page position [1]. The island of Corsica gives the name its adjective, but no source we checked explains the connection to sea, sky, or dye, so it is undocumented here [1].

In our color graph the nearest named neighbor is [[coolie|Coolie]], 4.0 units away [1]. A little further, at 4.5 units, is [[china-blue|China Blue]] [1]. The Munsell notation is 8.9PB 3.0/6.4, in the purple-blue wedge the ISCC-NBS calls "moderate purplish blue," which puts it near both our [[blue|blue]] and [[purple|purple]] families [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 0.13% of 23,781 paintings, 30 of them, as photographed, with the within-painting lens counting 15 [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a shadow, in 40% of its 15 appearances [2]. The earliest match dates to 1340, by Pietro Lorenzetti, 590 years before Maerz and Paul recorded the name, a floor rather than a first, since a color match in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment [2].
